🇲🇽🏙️ <u>Mexico City: Fewest Homicide Cases in 20 Years</u>

Mexico City opened 42 homicide investigations in September, the lowest monthly count in 20 years and the fourth straight month of record lows, Mayor Clara Brugada reported. Homicide cases are down 53% from 2019, and high-impact crime fell from 137 a day to 52. Meanwhile, the number of people charged with homicide each day is up 113% over 2019.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Names Its First Ambassador to Peru Since 2022</u>

President Sheinbaum designated career diplomat Lydia Antonio de la Garza, with more than 25 years in the Foreign Service, as Mexico's ambassador to Peru. Lima expelled Mexico's last ambassador, Pablo Monroy, in 2022 after AMLO refused to recognize Dina Boluarte. Relations broke entirely in November 2025, when Mexico granted asylum to former Peruvian Prime Minister Betssy Chávez, and were restored on August 7. The Senate must now ratify her.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Slaps $68.60 a Bike on Chinese Dumping</u>

The Economy Ministry imposed a provisional countervailing duty of $68.60 on every adult bicycle imported from China, effective October 13 for six months. The case file explains why: between 2022 and 2024, Mexican adult-bike production fell 34%, domestic sales 32% and jobs 29%, while Chinese bikes sold at prices 27% below Mexican manufacturers.

🇲🇽✊ "Happiness is not in money, as some think... it is in love for one's neighbor, love for the homeland and for family." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 12, 2026 Asked what the progressive left offers once the first stage of cutting poverty is done, Sheinbaum laid out the difference with the neoliberal period. "Before, they governed for a few. Economic power and political power were the same." Today, "the government represents the people, it does not represent a minority." Second, honesty and no corruption. Third, guaranteeing the rights to education, health and housing, along with freedoms, democracy, sovereignty and independence, "always with social justice." She cited López Obrador's latest book and philosopher Leopoldo Zea: some societies went the way of accumulation, "happiness associated with having more and more and more."

🇲🇽🔍 "What we saw yesterday, using water to break up a demonstration, must not happen in Mexico." "The right is authoritarian by definition. Even if they talk about democracy, their vision is authoritarianism." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 12, 2026 On Sunday, authorities in Jalisco used water jets and tear gas against people protesting at the state government house in Guadalajara over contaminated tap water. A Reporteros MX journalist read out 56 names of people reported detained. Sheinbaum said the Jalisco government must explain its decision and give the names of everyone detained. She recalled the 1968 massacre and the political disappearances of the 1970s: "Those who fill their mouths with the rule of law have to act according to the rule of law."

🇲🇽⚖️ "There are some who seek foreign interference, just like in the 19th century, when the conservatives went looking for an emperor to govern Mexico. They went looking for Maximilian." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 12, 2026 Asked whether recent reforms can shield Mexico from outside interference, after Brazil's first-round vote, Sheinbaum read Article 40 of the Constitution as amended last year: the people of Mexico will under no circumstances accept interventions from abroad, such as coups, interference in elections or violation of Mexican territory by land, water, sea or air. Article 19 now sets the maximum penalty for armed foreign agents. An election can be annulled for foreign interference, and presidents and governors may no longer hold dual nationality. "Today they act seeking outside interference because they don't have the strength to convince the people of Mexico."

🇲🇽🎨 "Education is the best tool against violence. That is why we have always defended public education." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 12, 2026 On Sunday Sheinbaum opened a campus of the Rosario Castellanos National University in Nicolás Romero, State of Mexico, built by the municipality, with the university providing teachers and curricula. Next year brings more high schools: technological schools, expanded campuses, middle schools without an afternoon shift turned into high schools, and the new Margarita Maza model. Public universities are opening more seats. The goal is over 350,000 additional university places by the end of the term, "like three UNAMs" of undergraduates. This year marks 40 years since the CEU student movement, where she came of age politically.

🇲🇽🔍 "What we do not agree with is supporting the privatization of the water service." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 12, 2026 Guadalajara's metro area is living with contaminated tap water. Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus proposed a financing scheme that, according to Conagua, involves private operation of the service; it needs two-thirds of the Jalisco Congress, where Morena legislators oppose it. Sheinbaum said the federal government is ready to share the cost and solve the problem technically, but not through privatization. In the last term López Obrador built the El Zapotillo dam; the aqueduct that the Jalisco government under Enrique Alfaro was to co-finance never came. "President López Obrador kept his word. Governor Alfaro did not keep his part."
